name: Nogai

ancestors.notes: Descent from Proto-Turkic (Kipchak branch, Kipchak-Nogai group).
Kumyk adstrate: neighbouring Kipchak-Cuman contact in the North Caucasus.
Russian adstrate: Soviet-era lexicon and administration.

notes: Nogai (ногай тили), a Kipchak Turkic language spoken in the North Caucasus and lower Volga, Russia, written in a Cyrillic alphabet reformed in 1960: the Russian letters plus the umlaut letters ⟨аь⟩ /æ/, ⟨оь⟩ /œ/, ⟨уь⟩ /y/ and the digraphs ⟨гъ⟩ /ʁ/, ⟨къ⟩ /q/, ⟨нъ⟩ /ŋ/, ⟨дж⟩ /dʒ/. Vowel harmony (front/back, rounding) operates throughout. ⟨ф ц щ ъ ь⟩ occur mainly in Russian loanwords; the silent hard/soft signs carry no independent segment and are omitted from the grapheme map. ⟨дж⟩ /dʒ/ is kept as its own grapheme key (not derived from ⟨д⟩ /d/ + ⟨ж⟩ /ʒ/) because it spells a single post-alveolar affricate phoneme, written with the same two-letter digraph convention in Kumyk (cf. Khakas ⟨ӌ⟩, Shor ⟨ҷ⟩ for the same segment with a dedicated single letter).
